reader.requirement: At --std 85, a Format 1 ACCEPT (FROM omitted, or FROM a mnemonic-name of a hardware device) must transfer data from the device and replace the whole content of identifier-1, for every receiver the 1985 formats allow (alphanumeric, alphabetic, numeric DISPLAY or COMPUTATIONAL, edited, group, subscripted, reference-modified, a group containing OCCURS DEPENDING ON), with the device-to-item conversion the implementor documents (DOC-A.1-1).

edition-consulted.switches: END-ACCEPT (construct end-accept-2002, COBOL0816) refused below COBOL-2002; outside the device transfer itself
ctx.Edition is only the diagnostic sink; the Format 1 device binding has no edition arm

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior in AcceptDisplayEmitter.cs, AcceptSource.cs and ReceivingStore.cs: no hit; the conversion form is the --numeric-display compile option, not the edition (DOC-A.1-1: 'at every --std').
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the device transfer and its conversion are the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_z05 covers alphanumeric receivers and an unsigned numeric DISPLAY receiver, with and without FROM; not exercised: alphabetic, signed, scaled, COMP, edited, group, ODO group, subscripted and reference-modified receivers

probes.expected: every receiver's prior content (all Z, 999, QQQ) is replaced; numeric receivers convert by the documented decimal form; an edited receiver stores the characters unedited (DOC-A.1-1)
an ODO group at 3 occurrences receives 6 characters; reference modification at (1:10), (10:1) and (4:) and a subscripted element receive exactly their positions
end of input leaves the receiver spaces, converting to zero (DOC-A.1-5); the 18-digit maximum takes 18 digits

probes.printed: error COBOL0817: ACCEPT FROM 'NO-DEV': not a mnemonic-name declared in SPECIAL-NAMES
error COBOL0817: 'SW1' is the mnemonic-name of the switch-name 'SWITCH-1', not of a device-name
probes.expected: refused: not associated with a hardware device (§1985:VI.6.5.3 SR1)

probes.printed: error COBOL0816: END-ACCEPT (explicit scope terminator) requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: refused at 85: the 1985 ACCEPT has no END-ACCEPT

probes.printed: error COBOL2269: unexpected 'ON'. ACCEPT ON EXCEPTION ...
probes.expected: refused at 85: no ON EXCEPTION phrase in the 1985 formats

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR1  (6.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1
OK  §1985:VI.6.5.3 SR1  (6.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: run_probe.py gives the program /dev/null as standard input, so the input-bearing runs executed the program run_probe built (runs/acc_kinds-002) as `dotnet acc_kinds.dll < acc_kinds.in` in that same run directory; the run_probe run itself is the end-of-input probe. COBOL0817 and COBOL2269 cite §2023 text at --std 85 (a diagnostic-wording matter, not this rule).

refuter.evidence: Read AcceptDisplayBinder.BindAccept (excluded receivers, the device arm) and checked DOC-A.1-1 (the implementor's conversion). Probes at --std 85 under runs/: acc_grp (input acc_grp.in, the built program run with input redirected): an 80-byte group ending in PIC S9(9) COMP stores the record byte for byte (G shows ...aaaaABCD back), a group with PIC 9(4) COMP stores its 8 leftmost characters, a signed SIGN LEADING SEPARATE item inside a group takes characters positionally; class a: a group J holding its own ODO object (JN=3 before the ACCEPT) takes 10 characters, its MAXIMUM length, which 1985 requires for a receiving group ('OK  §1985:VI.5.8.4 GR3b ... If the group is a receiving item, the maximum length of the group will be used'). class c: ACCEPT X FROM CONSOLE with no SPECIAL-NAMES refused COBOL0817 (acc_dev); FROM a mnemonic for SYSOUT refused 'not capable of input' (acc_outdev); a PIC N receiver refused COBOL0900 'requires COBOL-2002' (acc_nat). An index data item is refused (BindAccept line 80), as 1985 USAGE INDEX allows no ACCEPT reference. No receiver kept prior content. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR1  (6.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1'. Diagnostics cite §2023 text at --std 85: a wording matter, not this rule.
